items.item_text: Pharmacy Technician Certification (CPhT) from the Pharmacy Technician Certification Board (PTCB)
Experience in acquiring inventory from wholesalers, direct from manufacturers, or other vendors
Experience correctly and accurately using, maintaining, and troubleshooting pharmacy automation
Experience in inventory management at a Health System Outpatient Pharmacy or Specialty Pharmacy
Experience running reports and analyzing data for inventory requirements or optimizing system operations
Experience with 340B drug pricing program inventory management and 340B accumulator platforms
Experience with Microsoft Office software such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
Experienced in utilizing EPIC Willow Ambulatory pharmacy dispensing system
Project planning experience
Experience in non-sterile compounding tasks using equipment including, but not limited to: graduated cylinders, mortars and pestles, scales, stirring machines, etc.
Must be able to work and travel to ALL Outpatient pharmacies listed in this Job Description:
40% - Automation Operations
40% - Inventory Management
10% - Administrative Activities and Collaboration
5% - Quality Assurance and Compliance
5% - Performs Pharmacy Technician Functions as assigned
Current working knowledge of pharmacy terminology, generic/brand names and drug abbreviations
Working knowledge of current Medi-Cal Formulary and other third-party billing systems
Ability to recognize situations that exceed technician authority and ability and must be referred to a pharmacist for resolution

Problem-solving skills to independently recognize and define a problem and identify the resources available to help solve the problem, and to independently create and implement viable solutions and follow through to ensure the problem is resolved
Ability to exercise discretion to ensure that patient confidentiality is maintained, and a professional, respectful clinic/department environment exists at all times
Ability to impart knowledge and develop the skills of students participating in training programs, as well as new hires and staff seeking additional opportunities
Working knowledge of and skill to apply practices, principles and techniques of patient care related to area of expertise

Written and oral communication skills to provide information, explanations and instructions clearly and concisely to, and to elicit information from others with varying levels of ability to understand, including individuals who are ill or distressed, or who may not speak English
